sentence: This project uses physical models to study how known antibiotics kill bacterial cells, then uses machine learning to find classes of antibiotics.
This project studies why memory T cells in human skin need efficient protein translation to survive, which matters for chronic inflammatory skin diseases.
This project tries to find the mechanotransduction pathways that control how tendon develops under mechanical loading.
This project studies why changes in one protein raise the risk of primary open-angle glaucoma, using human cell lines and a mouse model.
This project studies how calcium signals in the embryonic zebrafish heart guide the way the heart develops.
This project builds a collection of human stem cell models of Alzheimer disease and related dementias to study how these diseases work.
This project studies how a signaling axis helps glioblastoma cancer cells invade the brain and resist treatment.
This project builds computer methods that use X-ray 3D imaging to plan histotripsy treatment of liver tumors and adjust for respiratory motion.
This project develops molecular imaging agents and tests them for use in humans, focusing on cancer, inflammation and immunity.
This project tests whether imaging plus a liquid biopsy test of circulating tumor cells shows which advanced prostate cancer patients respond to therapy.
This project studies how infection with Murine Roseolovirus in newborns leads to autoimmune gastritis later in life through type I interferon.
This project builds computer tools that use deep learning to analyze microbiome data, and runs biological experiments to learn how microbiomes affect health.
This project studies whether engineering T cells with a chimeric antigen receptor inside the body improves their quality and effect.
This project builds tissue engineered colorectal cancer spheroids that model human disease for drug screening.
This project uses artificial intelligence tools to find signs that separate milder influenza from severe influenza in patient data.
This project studies why states differ in pediatric hospitalizations and reported child maltreatment, and which policies could reduce them.
This project studies how fluorine changes the folding, activity and assembly of nucleic acids and nucleoproteins, and uses this to design chemical probes.
This project offers research cores that study aging through proteins, metabolism, invertebrate models and artificial intelligence.
This project tests engineered B cells in immune organoids from mice, non-human primate and human tissues to develop a cell therapy against HIV.
